title: Wrong Formula? Homogeneity Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Kilograms add to kilograms and minutes add to minutes, but nobody adds kilograms to minutes. That simple idea is a powerful test. Aarav's classmate writes a formula for how far a bicycle goes: x = ut + at. Is it even possible? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn the principle of homogeneity of dimensions and use it to catch a wrong formula in ten seconds.

A live bicycle simulation shows every term of x = ut + 1/2 at^2 growing in metres, with the x-t graph drawn beside it. We check the formula term by term, see why the classmate's at term is a speed and not a length, and prove why every term must match: measure the same ride in minutes and a mixed formula gives a different answer. Two pause-and-think questions cover why passing the check does not prove a formula right, and why whatever sits inside sin, cos, log or e must be a pure number. Then a worked example with v^2 = u^2 + 2as, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
